newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Global Carriers buys two ships.
newsitem.headline: Global Carriers buys two ships.

text.p: Malaysian shipping company Global Carriers Bhd said on Monday that it has, through its wholly-owned subsidiaries, acquired two bulk carriers for $7.65 million.
It said in a statement it has also signed an agreement to buy another vessel for $6.55 million.
One bulk carrier of 50,200 DWT built in 1976 was bought from a Liberian company for $5.4 million.
The other vessel, a 1974-built general cargo carrier of 15,180 DWT capacity, was acquired from a Panamanian company for $2.25 million.
The company expects delivery of a third bulk carrier in mid-September. The 18-year-old 115,000 DWT capacity ship is also owned by the Panamanian company, the statement said.
It said various incentives offered by the Malaysian government prompted it to acquire the ships.

The company said the government offered concessional finance to buy the ships, tax-exemption on income from Malaysian flag-vessels, accelerated depreciation on the ships and double tax deduction on related insurance premium.
"Global Carriers intends to fully and immediately capitalise on such incentives by increasing its fleet of vessels through the acquisition of second hand vessels," its statement said.
